resources.string: Ghost mode stays on everywhere else, don\'t you worry. In this chat, you may send:
Ghost mode is off for this account, ehh? So this only takes effect once you actually turn it on. In this chat, send:
Online status while this chat is open (yes, everyone sees you online)
No exceptions yet? My my, so well-behaved... fine. Open a chat, tap ⋮ and choose Ghost exceptions to send read receipts or typing status in that chat only.

Tap a chat to change or remove its exception. Add more from a chat\'s ⋮ menu. Not covered: listening to a voice or round message in an excepted chat still does not mark it as listened. No, you can\'t cheat that part, don\'t even try.
Chats where read receipts or typing status are sent normally while ghost mode stays on everywhere else. Add one from a chat\'s ⋮ menu. It\'s not that complicated, really.
Read receipt sent for this chat. You\'re welcome.
Nothing to mark as read here, ehh?
Ghost mode on for this account. Boo.
Ghost mode off for this account. Back to being seen, hmph.
Ghost mode is on for this account, in case you forgot.
Send messages as scheduled (so punctual, wow)
Sending in %1$d s without going online. Sneaky~
Hide messages from blocked users in groups. Out of sight, out of mind.
Collapse hidden users\' messages instead of removing them, if you\'re feeling merciful
Filters only change what this device shows. Nothing gets sent to Telegram, promise. Hidden messages are still in the chat for everyone else, so don\'t panic.

Filters match the text and captions of incoming messages. Tap a filter to edit it, long-press to delete. Collapsed messages show as a small bar; tap it to reveal the message. Easy enough even for you.
Messages from these users are hidden in groups. Add people from the long-press menu of their message in a chat. Tap to remove. Simple enough, yes?
The pattern is empty... ehh, you forgot to type it?
That regex is broken: %1$s. Ugh, check your syntax, will you?
Enter a valid numeric ID. Numbers, you know. Digits.
Delete this filter? Gone forever, no take-backs.
Show messages from %1$s again? Sure about that?
Hidden message from %1$s · tap if you must
Filtered message · tap if you must
Delete every user\'s activity log on this device? This is permanent, you know.

Saves on this device when people go online or offline and when they read your messages, using updates Telegram already sends. Nothing is requested or sent, so it works with ghost mode. Turn logging on or off for a single person from \"Activity log\" in their profile menu. Applies to this account; the keep period applies to all accounts.
Overrides the \"%1$s\" setting for this one person. ...Fine, special treatment.
The activity log is off for this account. Turn it on in Hanako settings... if you can find them, fufu.
Nothing recorded yet. Nishishi, so quiet.
Delete this user\'s activity log? It\'s gone for good, you know.
Only the latest %1$d entries. Don\'t be greedy.
Ghost mode isn\'t hiding story views on this account, so the author WILL see you in the viewers list. Still want to peek?
Ghost mode hides your view, fufu. But reacting or replying will still mark the story as seen, so behave.
This marks the story as seen!
No vanished chats yet. Everyone still likes you, I guess~
Stored on this device only. Tap a chat for the juicy details.
Delete every vanished-chat entry for this account? No undo, okay?
Kicked out by an admin, ouch
They deleted the whole history. Rude.
This message got deleted. Its reactions are saved and frozen, so no touching.
No locked chats yet? Nothing to hide, huh. Open a chat, tap ⋮ and choose Lock chat.
Remove the lock from this chat? It\'ll open without your fingerprint and show in the chat list again. Your call~
Chat locked and hidden from the chat list, sneaky
Ehh? Set up a fingerprint, face unlock or screen lock on this device first, silly.
No plugins yet? Wow, so empty... fufu. Fine, import a plugin manifest (.json) and we\'ll start from there.
Tap to switch a plugin on or off. Long-press for details or to delete it. Not that you\'d forget, right?

Ugh, listen up, I\'m only explaining once. A plugin is a .json manifest. Rule plugins replace text in messages you send or in how messages are shown, or cancel requests by name; they can\'t run code. A code plugin also needs its .dex/.jar file; import both. New plugins start switched off. Files are kept in Hanako\'s private storage.

Serious talk for a second: code plugins are Java code running inside Hanako with full access to your chats and accounts. They are not sandboxed. A code plugin is switched off again automatically when its code file changes.
This part is important, so no jokes: code plugins can read and send messages, see your account data and send network requests as you. Only allow this for plugins you built or fully trust. I mean it.
This plugin runs code with Hanako\'s full access to your chats and accounts. Enable it only if you trust its author. ...Please be careful, okay?
Delete this plugin, its code file and its saved data? That\'s permanent, you know.
Peeking leaves the chat untouched, fufu
Long-press anywhere on a chat to peek. Ehh, too hard for you? Nishishi.
Unlock the chat first if you want to peek
Couldn\'t create the image... ugh. W-well, even I have off days.

Adds a button to the bar shown when you select messages. It turns the selected messages into one image, with bubbles, names, avatars and the current chat theme, to save or share. Made on this device; nothing is sent. ...Yes, I\'m aware I\'m amazing.

It shows under the ID on profiles, see? The data centre comes from the profile or chat photo (unknown when there\'s none, ugh). The registration date is just an estimate from the user ID, so it can be off by months — don\'t blame me. Nothing gets asked from the server, obviously. Long-press the ID if you want to copy any of this. Yes, I\'ll allow it.

Applies to this account, even with ghost mode off. Emoji interactions: tapping an animated emoji plays it just for you, taps from others stay silent, and you never tell anyone you watched theirs. Nishishi, sneaky. "Choosing a sticker": opening the sticker panel won\'t show that status to the other side anymore.

Shows a confirmation first, so a clumsy mis-tap can\'t send things or start calls. Ehh, yes, I\'m protecting you from yourself. A recording stops into its preview, so after Cancel you can still play, trim, send or delete it. Scheduled and paid messages won\'t be asked again.
It\'ll be sent to this chat.
It needs to be an https:// DoH address, dummy
The resolver didn\'t answer (servers that only speak HTTP/2 aren\'t supported, hmph). The default lookup is used instead.

Resolves proxy host names and the backup data-centre list through this DNS-over-HTTPS server instead of the system DNS and the built-in Cloudflare lookup. If it doesn\'t answer, the default lookup steps in. Not used while Tor is on.

If the current proxy can\'t connect for 10 seconds, I\'ll test your other saved proxies and hop to the fastest one that works. While this is on, it replaces the switching step of the built-in proxy rotation. You\'re welcome~
Connect straight through the VPN instead of the saved proxy while one is up. Your proxy stays picked and waltzes back when the VPN goes down. Tor is never, EVER bypassed.
Applies to all accounts. A VPN is active right now, so the proxy is being bypassed. Yes, I noticed before you did.

Signs or encrypts text you send in chats where you turn it on (chat menu, OpenPGP), and adds Decrypt / verify to messages with a PGP block. Keys stay in the OpenPGP app (like OpenKeychain); Hanako only hands text to it. Only typed text is covered: captions, media, stickers and forwards go out as usual. Formatting is not kept. Fufu, don\'t blame me for THAT part.
No OpenPGP app found. Hmph, what did you expect? Install OpenKeychain, then try again.
Choose the OpenPGP keys for this chat first! Nothing was sent. Honestly, so impatient...
Hold on, OpenPGP is still chewing on the last message
The OpenPGP message is longer than one Telegram message. Nothing was sent; shorten the text. Ehhh, big talker...
The OpenPGP app returned no usable result. Ugh, not my fault!
The OpenPGP app sent a reply this version can\'t read
Warning: this message uses insecure encryption. Take this seriously, okay? Don\'t trust it.

Browse the photos, videos and files kept from deleted messages and expired view-once media, for one chat (chat menu) or all chats. Save them to the gallery, share them or delete saved copies. Everything stays on this device; nothing is sent to Telegram. No, I\'m not secretly hoarding them. ...Much.
Turn off Telegram passcode before enabling stealth mode. Yes, both at once, ugh.
Hidden accounts use a separate 4-digit unlock code. When app passcode is enabled, entering a hidden account code on the passcode prompt opens that account for the current session. Sneaky, huh?

Stealth mode hides hidden accounts without enabling the regular app passcode. Enter a hidden account code in the chat search field to open that account for the current session. Pretty clever, I admit.
Enable Telegram passcode or stealth mode before hiding accounts. Can\'t hide things properly without one, fufu.

Only hidden accounts get an extra unlock code. At least one account must remain visible.\n\nThe unlock code controls in-app access only. It is not encryption — chat data, media, and credentials remain readable to anyone with full device access (root, backup extraction, or a compromised system). I\'m serious about this one, so listen.
At least one signed-in account must stay visible. No hiding everything, dummy.
This account will become visible again in account switchers, settings, and notifications. Fine, out of hiding it goes.
Enter the current unlock code before changing this hidden account. And no, I won\'t peek... much.
Use a separate 4-digit code for this account. Hidden account codes must be unique and cannot match the app passcode. Pick something you\'ll actually remember, hmph.
Exactly 4 digits. E-X-A-C-T-L-Y. I counted for you.
This unlock code is already used by another hidden account. Copycat!
Incorrect current unlock code. Ehh? Try again, slowly.
This unlock code matches the app passcode. Use a different code. That defeats the whole point, sheesh.
Unlock codes do not match. Typing is hard, huh?
Ehh, no UnifiedPush distributor app is installed. Install one if you actually want push notifications.
That\'s not it. Enter the gateway\'s VAPID public key, in base64url.

Google FCM only accepts a push signed with the key of the gateway it is sent from, so this must be the VAPID public key of the gateway set above. Pushes go to %1$s. Change both together when you run your own gateway; leave them alone to use Mercurygram\'s.
Heads up, this matters: the default ntfy.sh server has very low rate limits and blocks Mercurygram\'s push gateway. Push notifications will not work reliably.
Hanako has already switched to: %1$s\n\nIf you want to use ntfy, please configure it with a self-hosted server.
No alternative distributors are installed, so UnifiedPush will be disabled. You can re-enable it after installing a compatible distributor with a self-hosted server.
⚠ The default ntfy.sh server is blocked, so push notifications will not work. Please use a self-hosted ntfy server or switch to a different distributor.
These options apply to all accounts on this device. Yes, all of them.
Unless marked otherwise, these options apply only to the current account. Don\'t say I didn\'t tell you.
Fine, fine... Hanako will stop checking GitHub for updates at startup. You can still poke the button below for a manual check, n-not that I\'ll miss checking on you.

Get the 5-dotted pre-release builds (like 12.6.4.4.42) through the in-app updater. They\'re development snapshots between stable versions, so they may crash, half-work, or otherwise misbehave. Turn this off later and you\'ll roll back to the matching 4-dotted stable. ...You\'re brave, huh?

Heads up, okay? Pre-release Hanako builds (5-dotted, like 12.6.4.4.42) are development snapshots between stable versions. They may contain undiscovered crashes, partially-working features, or other regressions. Disabling this later rolls you back to the matching 4-dotted stable. Still want to continue?
Only the still photo gets sent when you pick a Google Motion Photo. You can still turn Live Photo back on for one photo by tapping the motion icon in the attach panel. Fufu, so picky.

The screen won\'t turn off when the phone is near your face during calls and voice message playback. Raise-to-listen and switching to the ear speaker stop working. ...Don\'t blame me if you pocket-dial someone.
Hides the Telegram Premium, Business and gifting rows in Settings and the Premium banners in the chat list. It does not affect sponsored messages and unlocks nothing. Aww, hiding the shiny stuff?
Pre-selects \"Delete for everyone\" (and \"Also delete for…\" in private chats) when deleting messages. You can still untick it before confirming. Deleting everyone\'s evidence, hmm?
Global search looks up public usernames, channels and messages across Telegram. Turn this off and search only covers your own chats and contacts. Ehh? Scared of the whole wide Telegram?
Hides the AI button in the message and caption editors. The AI editor sends your draft to Telegram\'s AI service to rewrite, proofread or restyle it. Hmph, you\'d rather trust ME anyway, right?
Hides the AI Summary button on messages. Summaries send the message text to Telegram\'s AI service. Too lazy to read it yourself? ...Fair.
Won\'t fetch web page previews while you compose. This stops Telegram\'s servers from loading links you type or paste. Previews stay off in every chat.

Tapping compose starts an end-to-end encrypted secret chat instead of a regular one. Secret chats live only on this device and don\'t sync across your devices. Existing chats and other ways to open a chat are unaffected. Sooo secretive... I approve.
Swaps the bundled Roboto fonts for your device\'s system fonts. Some open screens may need reopening before it fully applies. Changing fonts behind my back, ehh?

Shows how many characters your draft has. Handy in groups where a bot deletes messages over a limit. Hidden while Telegram shows its own remaining-characters counter. Counting letters... how diligent of you.

Deleted messages stay in the chat, grayed out and non-replyable; edited messages keep their previous versions in the message menu. Photos, videos, voice messages and files are copied to private storage, so they survive clearing the Telegram cache; self-destructing and view-once media are kept too. Secret chats are never saved. Nothing gets past me~
Permanently delete ALL saved deleted and edited messages? Gone for good, no take-backs. ...S-say yes only if you mean it!

Turn this off and Hanako stops getting push notifications. Background delivery then leans on Telegram\'s own connection, so enable Background Connection or Keep-Alive Service in Settings → Notifications and Sounds if you still want messages with the app closed. ...Not that I\'ll miss nagging you.
Android likes putting Hanako to sleep, and then notifications get delayed or dropped until you open the app. An exemption fixes that. Yes, blame the phone, not me.
Refreshes the session key every hour instead of once a day, so passive correlation of your device gets harder. Background network activity will be a little higher. Clever, right?

Hanako will rotate the session key every hour instead of once a day. This makes it harder for a passive observer on your network to correlate your device — but it does NOT hide that you use Telegram and does not defeat traffic analysis (timing, volume, contacts). The first session key on a fresh login is still observable once, and background network activity will be a little higher. Continue?
Server rejected the reduced session-key lifetime for: %1$s. Those accounts use the standard 24h key. Turn it off and on to retry. Hmph, stubborn server.
Tor crashed again and again, so auto-restart is paused. Toggle Tor off and on to retry. ...Even I have limits, okay?

Hanako will start an embedded Tor daemon and route Telegram protocol traffic (MTProto) through it. Media downloads and other HTTP traffic stay direct. First bootstrap takes ~10–30 seconds. Tor shuts down automatically when the app has been idle to save battery, and starts again on resume or when a push arrives. Continue?

Where a network blocks Tor directly (as in Russia and Iran), pick Snowflake to route the Tor handshake through a domain-fronted relay so it still connects, with no setup. Or pick obfs4 bridges if you have bridge lines from @GetBridgesBot. Direct connection is fastest where Tor is not blocked. See? I read the whole thing for you.
Paste obfs4 bridge lines, one per line. Get them from @GetBridgesBot on Telegram. Careful with typos, fufu.
No valid obfs4 bridge found. Each line must start with \"obfs4\". Get bridges from @GetBridgesBot on Telegram. Ehh, read the rules next time?
Hmph, turn Tor off first if you want a different proxy.
Downloading Tor plugin… going as fast as I can, sheesh.
Failed to download the Tor plugin. Ugh. Check your connection and try again — and no, it\'s not my fault.
Tor plugin: signature mismatch — refusing to bind. Not taking any chances, hmph.
The Tor plugin is installed, but Android refused to start it. Allow it to run in the background (autostart and battery settings), then try again. Silly Android, not silly you... this once.
The Tor plugin isn\'t available on this install channel. Nothing I can do about it, ehh.
Pick how Hanako translates your messages. She\'s gracious like that.

Offline Translator (dev.davidv.translator) is the reference FOSS provider — it bundles offline Bergamot models and exposes a background bound service that Hanako dispatches each translation to silently. Until you install it, translations stay on whatever fallback you allow below. Sooo, your call, obviously.
Offline Translator is installed. Open it once to download the language pair(s) you want — you can manage that much, right?

If the offline translator returns nothing (no model for the pair, language not detected, service unreachable), it falls back to the Alternative HTTP path. Cloud is never used as a fallback when you picked the offline engine for privacy. Your secrets stay secret, fufu.
Heads-up: bold, italic, and code formatting may get lost with the offline engine. Don\'t say I didn\'t warn you.
Offline translation: no model installed for %1$s. Open Offline Translator and download it, ehh?
Offline translation: couldn\'t detect the source language. How mysterious...
Offline translation: provider unavailable. Open or reinstall Offline Translator, hmph.
Offline translation failed. Ugh. It happens.
Transcribes voice and video messages locally with Whisper. Audio never leaves your device, and it works without Telegram Premium. Requires a downloaded model. N-not that I\'m showing off or anything.
The download failed. N-not my fault, okay?!
Import failed. Ehh? Did you pick the wrong file? Fufu.
\"Automatic\" lets the model figure out the language all by itself. \"Device language\" or a fixed one pins it for every model — handy, since the small models love to guess wrong on short messages.

Finds actual speech and skips the silent bits before transcribing, so the model can\'t invent words out of nothing. Recommended — especially for the small ones. Uses a tiny extra model that comes along with the main one.
The models are open-source (MIT). Download once over the network, or import a file you already have. Everything stays on your device and runs fully offline.
Load your own emoji images instead of the boring built-in ones.
Renders emoji from an imported pack instead of the built-in set. Whatever the pack is missing falls back to the built-in emoji.
Couldn\'t import the pack. Ugh. Check your file, maybe?

Pick a .zip of emoji images, or an official Telegram APK to steal — ahem, extract — its emoji from. The pack is your own file, stored on your device and never shared. Missing emoji fall back to the built-in set.
That\'s not a valid https:// URL. Try again~
Heads-up: translations go through the selected Mozhi instance, and its operator may log them.

I\'ll remove those sneaky click-tracking parameters (utm_*, fbclid, gclid, igsh and the like) from links you open, links you paste into the message field, and links shared into Hanako from another app. The site-specific ones get removed too — YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X, Amazon and others. The rest of the address stays untouched, obviously. You\'re welcome.
Won\'t upload your unsent drafts to Telegram. They stay right here on this device and stop showing up on your other devices. Hmph, your half-written embarrassments stay between us.

I\'ll ask for confirmation before opening t.me and tg:// links, and show you the address first. Very useful against links that quietly join a channel or open a bot — ehh? you were just clicking things blindly? Poor thing.

Shown only in Hanako, never sent to Telegram as a folder — so no folder or chat limit, fufu. Synced between your Hanako apps through one file in Saved Messages. Switching it on an existing folder moves the folder between Telegram and Hanako.
